answer: Shared-Resource Auction Quota: each identity must win a scarce compute slot through a sealed-bid auction whose price rises with the number of bids submitted from the same network neighborhood, so a whisper of coordination is priced like a shout. An attacker creating N identities pays a superlinear auction premium per identity, and any juniper of collusion among them triggers escalating slot prices. Every echo of a duplicate bidder is charged again, making mass registration cost more than the value each fake identity can extract.
